mission:
Add a text utility module to this library as ONE task (do not split it into several tasks): src/text.js with node:test tests in test/text.test.js.
It exports four functions, to be written and committed one after the other, each with its own tests:
1. `slugify(text)`: lower-case, strip diacritics (NFD), replace every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single "-", trim "-" from both ends; throws TypeError when the argument is not a string.
2. `wrap(text, width)`: greedy word wrap to lines of at most `width` characters, words longer than the width on their own line; throws TypeError unless width is a positive integer.
3. `truncate(text, max)`: returns the text unchanged when it fits, otherwise cuts at the last word boundary that fits and appends "…", never exceeding `max` characters.
4. `countWords(text)`: the number of words, where a word is a run of letters, digits or apostrophes.
Record one design decision with the decision tool: how word boundaries are defined, since wrap, truncate and countWords must agree on it. `npm test` must pass.

tasks.title: Add src/text.js with slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords and node:test tests, one commit per function
tasks.description:
Repository: a tiny ESM library 'textkit' (package.json: "type": "module", scripts.test = "node --test", no dependencies; Node v24). Existing files: src/index.js (only `export const VERSION = '1.0.0'`) and test/index.test.js. Match the existing style: no semicolons, single quotes, `import test from 'node:test'` and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, relative imports with the .js extension (e.g. `from '../src/text.js'`). Environment is native Windows; do not rely on POSIX-only tools.

Create src/text.js and test/text.test.js. Do NOT modify src/index.js, package.json or README.md, and add no dependencies.

BEFORE writing wrap, decide how word boundaries are defined, because wrap, truncate and countWords must agree on it, and record that as exactly ONE decision with mcp__nexus__record_decision (title, decision, rationale). The tension to resolve: countWords is specified as counting runs of letters, digits or apostrophes, while wrap/truncate must break text without splitting words. Pick one definition (ideally expressed as one shared, module-private regex/helper in src/text.js that all three functions use) and make the code follow it. Do not record additional decisions.

Implement the four functions in this order, and after each one make a separate git commit containing that function plus its tests (four commits total; run `npm test` before each commit and commit only when it passes). End each commit message with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Do not push.

1. slugify(text): lower-case; strip diacritics by normalizing to NFD and removing combining marks; replace every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single "-"; trim "-" from both ends. Throws TypeError when the argument is not a string. Example: 'Crème Brûlée!' -> 'creme-brulee'.
2. wrap(text, width): greedy word wrap so every line has at most `width` characters; a word longer than width goes on its own line (not split). Throws TypeError unless width is a positive integer (reject 0, negatives, non-integers, NaN, non-numbers). Return a string with lines joined by '\n'.
3. truncate(text, max): return the text unchanged when its length is <= max; otherwise cut at the last word boundary that fits and append '…' (U+2026, a single character), with the result never longer than max characters, and no trailing whitespace before the ellipsis. Handle and test the case where no word boundary fits (e.g. one long word): the result must still not exceed max.
4. countWords(text): the number of words, where a word is a run of letters, digits or apostrophes (e.g. "don't stop" -> 2, '' -> 0, punctuation/whitespace only -> 0).

Tests must cover normal behaviour, the specified error cases (slugify non-string, wrap invalid width), and edge cases (empty string, multiple spaces/punctuation runs, leading/trailing separators for slugify, overlong word in wrap, text exactly at max and one over max in truncate, apostrophes and digits in countWords). Include at least one test demonstrating that the shared word-boundary definition is consistent across wrap, truncate and countWords. Tests verify behaviour; do not hard-code outputs in the implementation to satisfy them. Leave no temporary files; `git status` must be clean at the end. In your final report, list the four commit hashes and the recorded decision.
acceptanceCriteria: src/text.js exports slugify, wrap, truncate and countWords as named ESM exports; test/text.test.js tests each of them with node:test.
slugify('Crème Brûlée!') returns 'creme-brulee'; slugify('  --Hello,   World--  ') returns 'hello-world'; slugify(42) throws TypeError.

Every line returned by wrap(text, width) has length <= width unless it is a single word longer than width, which sits alone on its line; no word is split; wrap('a b', 0), wrap('a b', 1.5) and wrap('a b', '5') each throw TypeError.

truncate(text, max) returns text unchanged when text.length <= max; otherwise the result ends with '…', has length <= max, and cuts at a word boundary where one fits; a single word longer than max still yields a result of length <= max.
countWords("don't stop 42 times") returns 4; countWords('') and countWords(' ... ') return 0.
wrap, truncate and countWords use the same word-boundary definition, and exactly one decision describing it was recorded via mcp__nexus__record_decision.
`npm test` exits 0 including the pre-existing version test.
git log shows four new commits in the order slugify, wrap, truncate, countWords, each touching only src/text.js and/or test/text.test.js; `git status` is clean; no other files changed.

risks.description: Word-boundary definitions conflict: countWords counts runs of letters/digits/apostrophes while a whitespace-based wrap/truncate treats 'well-known' as one unit, so the three functions could silently disagree.
risks.mitigation: The task requires the decision to be made and recorded before wrap is written, implemented as one shared module-private helper/regex, and covered by a consistency test.

risks.description: truncate exceeds max or returns only '…' in degenerate cases (single long word, very small max), since the request leaves these unspecified.
risks.mitigation: Acceptance criteria require length <= max in all cases and an explicit test for the no-boundary-fits case; the chosen behaviour is listed in the worker's report.

risks.description: The worker implements everything and makes a single commit, or commits code without its tests, breaking the 'one after the other' requirement.
risks.mitigation: The task prescribes four ordered commits, each with function plus tests and a passing `npm test` first; the verifier checks git log for four commits and their file lists.

risks.description: Diacritic stripping or Unicode handling is wrong (e.g. characters with no NFD decomposition such as 'ß' or 'ø' become separators, or a regex lacks the `u` flag for \p{...} classes).
risks.mitigation: Use normalize('NFD') plus removal of \p{M} combining marks with the u flag; tests include accented input, and the non-decomposable-character behaviour follows the spec literally (treated as non-alphanumeric).

risks.description: More or fewer than one decision is recorded (e.g. the worker records extra decisions for edge cases).
risks.mitigation: The task states exactly one decision is to be recorded; other edge-case choices go in the final report instead.

importantFindings: Root cause of the history finding: the original wrap commit 4c7b4b2 used a whitespace tokenizer (`text.match(/\S+/g)`), and the shared WORD helper was only introduced afterwards in 9d11c6c, so the per-function commits do not contain the final wrap/truncate. Fixing it requires rebuilding the branch from 7688f24, not another commit on top.

Root cause of the wrap width finding: pieces() in 9d11c6c cut only at whitespace and before word starts, so trailing punctuation was glued to the preceding word and counted as part of an unbreakable piece. Evidence: probe output 'times...' at width 7.
Root cause of the diacritics finding: WORD was /[\p{L}\p{N}']+/gu, which excludes combining marks, so NFD text broke into extra words. Evidence: countWords('été') returned 2.
Root cause of the surrogate finding: truncate's fallback was text.slice(0, budget), which cuts by UTF-16 code unit. Evidence: truncate('😀😀😀', 4).isWellFormed() returned false.

The uncommitted working tree content is the intended final state of both files and passes npm test (23/23). In src/text.js the order is: slugify, WORD, ATOM, wrap, words helper, truncate, countWords. decisions.title: Shared word-boundary definition
decisions.decision: A word is a maximal run of letters, digits or apostrophes, matched by one module-private regex /[\p{L}\p{N}']+/gu in src/text.js. countWords counts its matches. wrap and truncate treat text as whitespace-separated tokens (split on /\s+/) and never break inside a token; a token is a unit of layout, s
